s01.narrative: The ministers repeat the confession — at Solemn Mass the deacon and subdeacon, otherwise the servers; the faithful join them, aloud at a dialogue Mass or in spirit.

s02.translation: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the Saints, and to you, father:

s03.translation: that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed:

s04.narrative: They strike their breast three times — a visible gesture of contrition accompanying the words of self-accusation.

s05.translation: through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault.

s06.translation: Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, all the Saints, and you, father, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

w001.function: It opens the prayer and governs the long chain of datives that follows — I confess: to whom?

w002.function: The one confessed to — first of the chain of datives after “Confíteor” (w001). Compare “Deum” (w065) — the same word in the accusative, in a different role.

w005.function: The next addressee of the confession in the list.

w006.function: An adverb modifying a noun, unusually: “semper Virgo” — “ever Virgin” — a fixed Marian title treated as a unit.

w008.function: Agrees with the name that follows, “Michaéli” (w009).

w010.function: Apposition to “Michaéli” (w009): same case, because an apposition inherits the case of the noun it restates.

w011.function: Agrees with the following “Joánni” (w012). “Beatus” recurs before each name in this litany of saints.

w016.function: Apposition to “Apóstolis” (w015) — the Apostles named one by one.

w021.function: Closes the list and adds its last member: the priest at the altar.

w022.function: Closes the chain of addressees: I confess also to you — the priest at the altar.

w023.function: Vocative, not the dative “patri” — a direct address to the person, not another item in the list; spoken to the priest.

w024.function: Introduces the content of the confession: “that I have sinned” — though the classical “for I have sinned” still resonates here.

w025.function: A completed act whose effect endures — hence the confession.

w027.function: By what have I sinned — by thought; first of three ablatives of means: by thought, by word, by deed.

w032.function: The written form does not distinguish the nominative (culpă) from the ablative (culpā) — sense decides: ablative of cause, “through my fault”. The familiar English “through my fault” renders it exactly.

w033.function: Agrees with “culpa” (w034) — the second of the three repetitions.

w035.function: The third and strongest repetition — “máxima” (w036) is about to join it.

w037.function: The threefold “mea culpa” builds: fault — fault — greatest fault.

w038.function: The prayer's logical turn: having confessed, I now ask for intercession.

w039.function: It takes an accusative of the person plus an infinitive: I beseech whom — to do what. Hence the whole list of saints now returns in the accusative.

w040.function: Agrees with “Maríam” (w041). Compare “beátæ” (w004): there dative after “Confíteor” (w001), here accusative after “precor” (w039).

w041.function: No longer the addressee of the confession but the one beseeched to intercede — object of “precor” (w039). Compare “Maríæ” (w005).

w042.function: In the fixed title “semper Virgo”, as in the first half of the prayer.

w043.function: Compare “Vírgini” (w007) — the same formula, there in the dative.

w056.function: Compare “Sanctis” (w020) — the same formula in the dative.

w058.function: Compare “tibi” (w022): the same person (the priest), a different case for a different role.

w059.function: The vocative repeated from the first half — addressed to the priest; hence “pater”, not “patri”.

w060.function: Infinitive in the construction “precor + accusative + infinitive”: I beseech them to pray. It carries the content of the petition.

w064.function: Accusative after “ad” (w063); the whole phrase “Dóminum Deum nostrum” stands in the accusative.

w065.function: Apposition to “Dóminum” (w064): the Lord — God. Compare “Deo” (w002): the same word opened the prayer in the dative; the prayer closes as it began.
